sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Candidate faithfully targets ships, validates every linked lookup case, requires the Table 6-6 and Table 6-7 cases and their respective selection keys/results, enforces exactly one table reference per case, and compares iceLoadCycleCount against k1*k2*k3*N_class*n_n using an expected-result-scaled tolerance with canonical datatypes and units.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: The qualifiedMinCount shapes only prove that at least one conforming Table 6-6 case and one conforming Table 6-7 case exist; additional applicable linked cases can be malformed and silently ignored. Add a constraint applied to every node reached through hasTableLookupCase that requires class tableLookupCase and exactly one tableReference, and conditionally requires iceClass plus selectedIceClassCycleCount for every case referencing traficomTable6Dash6 and tableLookupPropellerLocation plus selectedPropellerLocationFactor for every case referencing traficomTable6Dash7. Retain the two existence checks and formula comparison. Also remove the unsupported sh:nodeKind sh:IRI restrictions on lookup cases and selection-key values unless an IRI requirement is explicitly declared; the contract requires the supplied classes, not IRI-only representation.

Candidate faithfully targets ships, validates every linked lookup case, requires the Table 6-6 and Table 6-7 cases and their respective selection keys/results, enforces exactly one table reference per case, and compares iceLoadCycleCount against k1*k2*k3*N_class*n_n using an expected-result-scaled tolerance with canonical datatypes and units.
